replies.author: @kobiguru024
replies.text: During the Sultanate period, and even during the Mughal era (during the time of Shaista Khan), when Europeans came to this region, they used to compare it to paradise. Everyone among them wanted to come here. The problem isn't the country itself—no one else in the world possesses the fertile land that Bangladesh has—nor is population the issue. A country's population is extremely vital for it; in Europe, various companies are shutting down due to a shortage of people, because businesses revolve around human beings. Moreover, in the Middle Ages, Bengal was even more densely populated than others. The problem lies with a few greedy individuals who loot a massive portion of the nation's economy to feather their own nests, along with a few oligarchs misusing the country's resources, and some corrupt politicians and government bureaucrats. Their number might be around 500,000, but it is they who have kept 180 million people impoverished.
